questions.a: AI reputation management uses software to monitor, analyze and respond to what customers say about your business online. It pulls reviews and mentions from sites like Google, Yelp and TripAdvisor into one place, reads the sentiment behind them, and drafts replies for you. That frees your team from treating review replies as a full-time job.

questions.q: Why does reputation management get harder as you add locations?
questions.a: Reviews pile up across many platforms and every location, so there's no single place to see them all. Replying to each one and winning back unhappy customers takes far more time than a small team can give. Without structured analysis, it's also hard to tell what guests really think or which stores are slipping.

questions.q: What should I look for in AI reputation management software?
questions.a: Start with three basics: it should unify reviews from every platform and location, help you respond at scale, and surface insights about guest experience and operations. Beyond that, check whether it fits your industry and size, since some tools are built for local service businesses and others for large enterprises. Features like listings management, surveys and social listening matter if you plan to use them.

questions.q: Is social listening the same as review management?
questions.a: They overlap but cover different ground. Review management focuses on collecting reviews and replying to them, while social listening tracks brand mentions across social media, news, blogs, forums and podcasts. If catching conversations early matters to you, a listening tool adds coverage that a review inbox doesn't.

questions.q: How much does AI reputation management software cost?
questions.a: Pricing varies widely. Tools for small businesses often publish monthly plans, while enterprise platforms usually quote a custom price based on your number of locations and the features you need. Experience management suites aimed at large CX teams sit at the top of the range, so it's worth getting a quote for your exact setup.

questions.q: Which AI reputation management tool suits a multi-location restaurant brand?
questions.a: Look for a platform built for restaurants that handles reviews, replies and analytics in one place. Momos brings reviews from every location and platform into a Unified Inbox, uses its AI agent Alfie to write on-brand replies, and shows what drives positive and negative reviews at each store. You can also send surveys to collect more reviews from happy guests.
